In this past life recollection, I realized I was the child of a slave working on the farm of a noble family in the kingdom of Macedonia. My master's name is Dimitris, and he is an official who oversees the finances of King Philip II's court. This was the time when slavery flourished. Most slaves were prisoners of war captured in wars between neighboring city-states and territories. The law at that time did not allow slaves to have their own property but had to live under the control of their master. Depending on the owner's treatment, a slave's life will be comfortable or miserable. Female slaves had to do daily chores in the house such as cooking, washing, cleaning, serving or whatever their master requested. Male slaves had to do harder work such as farming, growing crops, building or looking after livestock.

My mother was a Thrace native who was captured during the war between Macedonia and Thrace.

She was sold at the slave market and bought by Dimitris. I didn't know who my father was, but when I began to understand, I heard the slaves say from far and near that master Dimitris was my father, although my mother never said anything about this.

I also asked my mother a few times, but every time she was silent or talked about something else. On the large farm of master Dimitris's family there were many slaves, male and female, and some were married and had children. These children played carefree with each other, not knowing anything about their slave status or that of their parents, until they were old enough and had the labor power to do the work of slaves like their parents.

As for me, since childhood I have noticed the difference in life between slaves and masters. This difference has kept me thinking. We children were confined to the slave quarters and were not allowed to go to our master's quarters. My mother said it was no place for people like us. I asked my mother, what's different about "people like us" than other people, but my mother couldn't answer. No one can answer that question of mine.

When I was five years old, I witnessed an event that made me begin to fear for my slave status.

Owner Dimitris often organizes parties and invites friends from other places to eat, drink, and have fun. Of course, these parties were all performed by the slaves in the house, because at a young age, I and the other slave children in the house were still able to have fun while learning how to do chores. Although we were not allowed to set foot in the area where the owner's parties were held, we still often secretly found a corner to observe these lavish parties. For us children, it was the joy of discovering another world. These parties often last until nearly midnight. When the party ended, the male slaves were allowed to leave the party room to return to the slave quarters, but the female slaves had to stay and continue serving these guests. I don't know what happened at night because the banqueting area was closed and there were guards. When morning came, the female slaves left looking sullen, tired, unsteady on their steps, and some even sobbed. What caught my attention is that every time this happened, the husbands of these women often showed hostility, anger, and sometimes fights broke out.

That time, after such a party, the husband of a female slave used too much force, injuring his wife. This story reached the owner's ears. The soldiers were called in, arrested the man and led him away from the camp. The next day, his body was hung on a wooden stake in the middle of the field for the birds and crows to nibble on. Looking at the bloody body covered in whip marks, we children were extremely scared. I worriedly asked my mother and she cried and said that it was a punishment for people who did not know their status as slaves. After witnessing the death of the man who still lived with us every day, I became more scared and cautious, and could no longer play freely like before.

Thoughts about slavery began to take root in me.

As for master Dimitris, he has three children, Sophia and Isidora are the two eldest daughters and Leonidas is the youngest son. Dimitris's wife died giving birth to Leonidas, so my mother, still young, was called to look after and care for his three children. Not long after, she gave birth to me. I lived in the slave quarters until I was six years old, when one day master Dimitris came to my mother, telling her that his son needed friends to play with, and I was chosen to be Leonidas's friend. From there, I was taken out of the slave area and returned to live in my master's big house. While living with my master's family and playing with his children, I didn't notice any differences between us. I was innocent at a young age, but sometimes I wondered why I could enjoy such comforts but other slave children could not?

Dimitris was one of the excellent students of the sage Plato in Athens. He was best at math, so he was invited by King Philip to look after the court's finances. Dimitris focuses on educating his children from a very early age. From a young age, Leonidas was taught mathematics, literature, sports... but Leonidas only liked music. As a slave and friend of Leonidas, I often stood in the room while Dimitris taught his children, so I learned a little. I really like math and often secretly help Leonidas when he can't solve difficult math problems. This did not escape the master's eyes, once he angrily scolded his son: "Even a slave like Kyros is better at math than you." Even though he said that, he never scolded me. Many times I caught him looking at me with puzzled eyes.

Some generals wanted Attalus, who was in command of the army, to become king. The court officials supported the musketeer commander, Amyntas, to ascend the throne. Both had military forces and held important roles. As for Alexander, although he did not have an army in his hands, Alexander could rely on the soldiers being trained in the martial arts school under the command of his friends Leonidas, Antigonus, Ptolemy, Seleucus, Hephaestion, Cleitus, Simonides and Philotas. As Dimitris's assistant, in charge of the army and weapons, I witnessed this historical event from beginning to end.

To regain complete sovereignty, Alexander took decisive action. That day, the young king entered the training camp, in front of thousands of soldiers, he began an eloquent speech talking about the gods, from Zeus, Apollo to Hercules, then talking about heroes like Achilles, Menelaus, Hector, Diomedes... with a loud voice, he quoted heroic poems in the epic Iliad that most young soldiers knew by heart. He mentioned the humiliation of Greece being invaded by Persia, about the destruction of sacred temples and ancestral tombs, and the occupied seas and islands, leaving the Greeks with no more fish to eat. He raised the question that if the kings and other leaders were still indifferent, only worried about competing interests, not seeing the danger of Persian invasion, could those old officials take on the responsibility of unifying the alliance to fight Persia? He believes that it is time for Greece to change and regain control of its future. Finally, he called on young people to step forward to take responsibility, shoulder the burden of national affairs, and build a strong future for Greece, instead of continuing to live in fear of the disaster of foreign invasion. Alexander's enthusiasm and enthusiasm touched all the soldiers and raised their morale. Even though I was a slave, I also felt a surge of enthusiasm in my heart, wanting to contribute to the restoration of Greece.

With that enthusiastic spirit, Alexander led his army straight into Pella to crush the factions of court officials who did not obey him. The quick march caught those people off guard. Amyntas was killed by Ptolemy before he could even put on his armor. Within half a day, the group of young soldiers took control of the situation in Macedonia.

Attalus, stationed on the outskirts, heard news of the upheaval in Pella and immediately led his army back to the court, but on the way, Alexander ambushed and killed him. In the harem, Queen Olympias also ordered all of King Philip's concubines to be killed. After internal liquidation, Alexander called a meeting of his generals and declared:

- My father is an idealist. He advocated uniting small states into a common bloc to fight against foreign invaders and then bring troops to reclaim the Greek ports that had been invaded by Persia. Now that my father has passed away, a number of countries have withdrawn from the alliance. Obviously, if Persia invades, we cannot rely on those countries. That's why the Khoi alliance is not strong enough. I have a realistic policy, I want to unify all countries into a single country, with a single military force, under the command of only one person, which is me!

Cheers rang out, showing everyone's unanimity at the young king's vigor. To prepare for war, the number of weapon forging factories was increased four times compared to before. My work is even busier than before, I have to constantly travel between factories to check, review, and make sure there are no errors in expenses. I'm so busy, but every time I stop somewhere and hear Lydia's melody from near and far, I can't help but remember Isidora and feel bitter about my slave status.

Alexander's war to unify Greece began with an attack on Thessaly, the most prosperous commercial center at that time. After only a few days of fighting, the Macedonian army was victorious. Alexander annexed Thessaly into Macedonia. The young king ordered all the men of this country to join the army, so the number of Macedonian troops increased significantly. Thessaly's boats and commercial assets were all confiscated and put into the royal treasury. To supplement the budget for military food and weapons, Alexander captured Thessaly women and sold them to slave markets. This was the first time I witnessed people buying and selling people like animals. I couldn't help but think of my mother who had suffered the same fate in the past. Looking at innocent people locked in animal cages, being sold in the human trafficking market, my heart was filled with a painful feeling like I was being mistreated. This is a strange feeling of pity and fear that I can't even explain. In Greek society, buying and selling slaves was normal. Most people take it for granted because class discrimination allows those in power to behave like that. Slaves also got used to this unfair treatment and had to accept their fate. How their lives turn out depends entirely on the owner's attitude. Most were treated brutally and only a few lucky people like my mother and I were treated more kindly. I still know "win to be the king, lose to be the enemy" but looking at the pain and suffering that the losers have to endure, my heart is extremely uncomfortable.

Looking at my shock at this scene of slave trading, Dimitris calmly said:

- This is the first time you've witnessed this, right? Calm down, don't be afraid.

In the future, you will witness many more terrible things.

I tried to calm down, but my words were still shaking:

- But why... why... did we do that?

Dimitris explains:

- Our purpose is to arm the army to fight the Persian threat. We need a lot of money to produce more weapons, so we have to force women to sell into slavery to supplement the budget. “The end justifies the means”, we have to do that. But don't be afraid, I will never sell you.

I nodded but didn't answer. Dimitris's unintentional words made me feel a bit bitter. Even though I was treated kindly, in Dimitris's eyes I was still just a slave, nothing more and nothing less. Being aware of my slave status, I was extremely grateful to Dimitris for bringing me home to live with his children and also teaching me an apprenticeship. However, sometimes I still feel a little bitter because, after all, Dimitris did all of that for his own benefit and he forever only considered me a slave. But why are some people born as slave owners and others born as slaves? Even though I can't currently explain my fate, in my heart, I still feel something urging me to find the answer.

After the victory at Thessaly, Alexander issued an ultimatum to the surrounding countries:

"Incorporate Macedonia or be conquered". Not receiving a response, the young king sent his army to Illyria, burned down the capital, and annexed the small country into Macedonia. Taking advantage of the victory, he pulled his army across the Shika Pass, completely obliterating the lands of Triballi and Getae, merging these two places into two provinces of Macedonia. With the strategy of rapid advance, with an enthusiastic army for the ideal of unifying Greece, in just a short time, Alexander conquered most of the surrounding countries.

Alexander is not only a good commander but also a talented strategist. Every time he conquered a country, he left behind a corps of soldiers from the Macedonian army to control security, while the entire army of that country would be merged into the main army of Macedonia. Each new soldier will be responsible for training by two Macedonian soldiers.

Soldiers are trained quickly and then immediately have to join the main force and immediately move to another country, so they have no choice but to fight under the Macedonian flag.

After conquering all neighboring states, Alexander planned to attack the two most influential countries in Greece at that time, Athens and Thebes. General Antipater proposed to launch troops to attack Athens first. Alexander laughed loudly:

- A country where every decision is made by dozens of people in parliament can never accomplish anything. Those useless people in parliament only talk but can't do anything. Just show the consequences of disobeying me and they will surrender without even having to fight.

Then Alexander ordered the army to gather and move to Thebes. This time, the young king had more than thirty thousand soldiers in hand, with twenty mobile fortresses erected to overcome the fortified wall of Thebes. The war lasted more than ten days with heavy losses on both sides, but in the end Alexander's army won. To deter Athens, Alexander ordered the Thebes palace to be burned to the ground. More than six thousand people's houses were also burned, thirty thousand people of this country were forced into slavery. The king also allowed soldiers to freely loot and kill as a reward for this bloody war. Two weeks later, when Dimitris and I brought supplies here, the fire that destroyed the capital had not yet gone out. Everywhere, human corpses were lying around, filling the fields, and the stench was strong. Flocks of vultures and black crows surrounded the bodies.

All created a truly horrifying scene.

I once believed in the young king's vision of uniting Greece to fight against foreign invaders and also accepted the view that "the end justifies the means" with forcing people to sell into slavery to get money to produce weapons. However, witnessing the destruction of an entire country, the plundering of wealth and the barbaric slaughter of innocent people just to prove power, I began to wonder if this whole thing was not only aimed at fighting foreign invaders but also about Macedonia's ambition to expand its territory? King Philip as well as Alexander both used fighting Persia as a just cause for the war, but behind that good ideal, did they both have their own ambitions for power?

In the Greek city-states, each city-state had its own unique cultural features and strengths. Thessaly is famous for trade, Sparta is strong in the military, Thebes specializes in livestock, Triballi specializes in maritime activities, Illyria specializes in agriculture and Athens is famous for culture. Macedonia is the poorest country because of its arid land conditions. It is thanks to the control of King Philip and Alexander that they have now conquered those city-states. Alexander redrawn the map, no longer dividing it into many countries, all became provinces of Macedonia.

When I look at this map, I think of Aristotle's teachings: "For everything, you must know how to ask "why" to find out the root cause", then wonder why those countries could be conquered so easily? Of course, everyone knows the young king's commanding skills, but I think if the people of those countries knew how to be independent, self-reliant, and determined to protect the country, if the kings of those countries ruled with justice instead of just enjoyment, how could Alexander easily conquer them?

It was because the leaders of those countries did not pay attention to running government affairs, did not focus on defense but only worried about enjoyment, so Alexander took advantage of the loophole and unified Greece. okay.

Just as Alexander predicted, the terrible fate of Thebes terrified the Athens parliament and immediately surrendered. Alexander sent a letter to Demosthenes, the letter was titled: "Dear Chairman of the Parliament, please let me know clearly: this "little boy" has unified Greece." Instead of killing Demosthenes, Alexander ordered the parliament to ordain him as the supreme leader of Greece and this must be celebrated in Athens, organized by Demosthenes himself.

Within just two years after ascending the throne in Macedonia, Alexander unified Greece into a single country. He promulgated a policy of centralization and all conquered city-states became centrally controlled provinces. He merged the armies of the countries into one block, placing them under his command, to prepare for war with Persia.

Alexander appointed General Antipater as regent, to oversee everything in Greece, and set up headquarters in Athens to oversee the parliament there. Being an intelligent man, Alexander did not believe that the Athenians truly obeyed him. Intellectuals who are proud of this country's democratic tradition will not easily accept a person from Macedonia, which they consider a barbaric country, to take over as their leader. This is not strange. Even when Athens surrendered, General Memnon, commander of the Athenian army, even led his troops to Persia, asking to join the Persian army to deal with Macedonia. This clearly shows the spirit of division and local selfishness of the Greek city-states at that time. However, Alexander's somewhat brutal determination, combined with his outstanding military talent, eventually turned Greece into a unified bloc, temporarily under the rule of the centralized government he proposed. The pacification of Greece completed, Alexander quickly took the next step on his war path. The young king gathered his forces, preparing to attack Persia.

Before leaving, Alexander and his classmates went to Mieza to say goodbye to his teacher, Aristotle. I was also brought along by Leonidas. The young king said to his teacher:

- I decided to attack Persia to clear away the hatred when this country used to send troops to burn down temples and trample on our ancestors' mausoleums. I will raise the Macedonian flag high throughout the Persian territory and bring Greek civilization to teach those stupid barbarians.

Aristotle looked at Alexander thoughtfully, then shook his head, calmly said:

- To conquer a country, it is not possible only by military force but must have a combination of three factors: military, economic and cultural. Without one of these three elements, you cannot rule anywhere for long. You should remember, military conquest is not difficult, what is difficult is conquering people's hearts. Although Persian civilization is different from ours, it is not necessarily inferior. You should not be too arrogant or underestimate values ​​that you do not understand clearly. To truly conquer a country, you must know how to respect their customs and culture, and treat the people there fairly, then you can win people's hearts. When the lives of the people of that country are comfortable, they will not oppose you. When the cultural customs of that country are respected, they will not consider you an invader, and only then will you succeed.

Alexander thought about what his teacher had just said. Being an intelligent person, he immediately understood that Aristotle was right, so he respectfully said:

- Your words are not wrong. You will listen to me, and when you march, you will bring along the best Greek scholars to study the customs and culture of other countries.

These people will help you adjust your governance appropriately.

Aristotle nodded. He thought for a moment, then said:

- If so, I will let Timotheus follow and help you. If you have any difficult problems, you can ask Timotheus or write to me.

Timotheus was also Plato's student at the Platonic Academy. When Plato died, Aristotle was not appointed abbot and had to leave Athens. Timotheus followed and became his close student. Timotheus' personality was deep and quiet, different from the enthusiastic and rowdy students like Alexander, Cleitus, Leonidas, Perdicas or Ptolemy. In addition, Timotheus was often asked by Aristotle to take his place in teaching, so everyone admired him and considered him a potential replacement for Aristotle.

Allowing his most trusted student to follow Alexander proves that Aristotle considered conquering the hearts and minds of Persia to be extremely important. This may also be partly because Aristotle did not want Alexander to be influenced by scholars from the Platonic Academy who followed the expedition.

Aristotle added:

- You also know that Greek civilization originated in Egypt, because Sinuhe, a sage from Egypt, came here to open a teaching school. However, Sinuhe only learned a part of the essence of Egypt, there was much more that he had not learned. Therefore, since ancient times, our country's sages such as Iamblichus, Pythagoras, Thales, and Solon had to go to Egypt to study further. I also want to go there to learn more like the ancients did. Unfortunately, Egypt was invaded by Assyria, then became a colony of Persia, so I don't want to go there anymore.

Alexander said immediately:

- Don't worry, after conquering Egypt, I will collect all the valuable books and documents of this country and bring them to Mieza for me to study.

Aristotle turned to the other students and kindly advised:

- Remember the teachings of ta. Never be complacent about what we already know. The learning pool is vast, there are countless things we don't know. What you know can cover what you see. Therefore, we need to avoid narrow-minded prejudices and should know how to observe everything, broaden our horizons, and be ready to experience and learn new things. Only then will you be worthy of being my students.

Having witnessed the conversation between Aristotle and his students, I deeply admired the wisdom of this sage. Although the battle had not yet begun, both Alexander and Aristotle believed that Macedonia would win. Knowing that no student is equal to his teacher, although he knew that the student had great ambition and had the talent to command and lead, Aristotle was also afraid that the enthusiasm and enthusiasm of that youth could lead to irreparable mistakes, so he sent his most trusted and talented student, Timotheus, to follow Alexander, to help rule the colonies more effectively and steadfastly.

To prepare for the great expedition, Alexander appointed Parmenion, the loyal general who once established Many victories of King Philip, as commander of the expeditionary army, then assigned friends such as Hephaestion, Perdicas, Leonidas, Ptolemy, Antigonus, Cleitus, Seleucus, Philotas and Simonides to hold other important positions. These people are all descendants of noble Macedonian families. Since childhood, they have been Alexander's playmates and grew up studying with Aristotle, so Alexander can count on their absolute loyalty.

Before the war, it was always a time when many young people rushed to get married. Partly because they want to enjoy their married life before the future falls into uncertainty, partly because families want to have children and grandchildren to continue the family line as soon as possible, because no one knows how unpredictable war and swords are. This is also the time when noble families arrange for their daughters to marry people who may hold important positions in the court in the future.

As a wise calculation person, Dimitris immediately arranged for Isidora to meet and betroth to Cassander, the son of general Antipater. Sophia was betrothed to Philotas, son of General Parmenion. Among Aristotle's students, these were the two people with the most future, both close friends of Alexander and the children of two generals commanding the Macedonian army. Sophia's wedding to Philotas was celebrated soon after, while Isidora's was postponed until winter. However, at the last minute, Antipater changed his mind and did not want his son to follow the expedition. To avoid criticism of his loyalty to Alexander, he arranged for Cassander to marry Alexander's sister Thessalonike, and then gave Cassander the position of administrative controller in Athens, ensuring that many of Alexander's family held power in an important place. This pleased Alexander and Queen Olympias, but it meant that the engagement with Isidora had to be canceled.

For Greek customs, this is no small scandal. In the Egyptian aristocracy, no matter what the reason, it was humiliating for a girl to be divorced.

Among the royal ladies, Isidora was famous for her beauty and was always sought after by many people. Leonidas's friends such as Simonides, Perdicas, Philiteus, and Medius also paid more or less attention to her. With such beautiful beauty, Isidora is also hated and envied by other ladies. Therefore, this unexpected divorce created a lot of gossip and spread very quickly. Dimitris was upset but couldn't do anything because Antipater was the general commanding the Greek army, and the regent, second only to Alexander. Furthermore, Thessalonike was a princess and Alexander's younger sister, so this marriage was considered a political game by Antipater, to become close to the royal family and gain Alexander's trust.

When I heard this unexpected news, my heart was so overwhelmed. Having lived close together since childhood, I knew that Isidora was still proud of her beauty and always wanted to marry a prestigious husband, so this must have been a huge shock for her. Of course someone like you would never pay attention to a lowly slave like me. However, facing this unfortunate incident, I feel sorry for her but I also secretly hope that one day she will change her mind...

At this time, Persia was a large empire, its territory stretching from Egypt to the mountains

Hindu Kush. Meanwhile, Greece is just a small peninsula. Many years ago, Greek ports such as Ephesus, Miletus, and Halicarnassus located on the other side of the Mediterranean were occupied by Persia. After that, the islands around Greece were gradually invaded. Persian ships controlled the important shipping lanes of the Mediterranean and attacked any Greek ships that dared to set sail. For nearly a century, the Greek people lived in fear of Persian expansion. They saw the Assyrian empire destroyed, the land of Kush wiped out, half of Nubia falling under Persian control, so most Greeks were filled with fear, not knowing when their country would be invaded and what their fate would be if they had to live under the rule of people they considered barbarians and barbarians.

In the past, King Philip of Macedonia advocated launching a war to unify the forces of the countries in the Greek peninsula in order to recapture the ports lost to Persia as well as to prevent being attacked again by Persia. However, when Alexander unified Greece, this young king, who had just turned twenty years old, advocated attacking Persia to completely end the threat of invasion that had existed since the previous century. With eloquent speeches about the heroic tradition of Greece, Alexander went everywhere calling for attacks on historical enemies, making young men passionately believe in the slogan "Fight first, win". Therefore, in just a short time, Alexander had more than forty thousand soldiers ready to fight.

Alexander reorganized the army according to a rapid march strategy to be ready to respond to all circumstances. Soldiers were trained to use very long sarissa spears to advance and retreat to the beat of the war drums, rather than fighting in an unstructured, rushing fashion like in the past. He also established a large-scale logistics system with many horse-drawn carriages to be able to move faster.

In addition, he brought with him many engineers to build roads, set up machines to shoot arrows, stone launchers, blacksmiths to cast weapons and also brought along a number of artists and musicians to stimulate fighting spirit*.

General Medius was assigned to oversee logistics. Dimitris was assigned the task of controlling military provisions, which required him to travel between the capital Pella and the places where Alexander was stationed. The trip could last a whole month, sometimes by boat, sometimes by road, through rolling hills and mountains, so Dimitris, citing old age and weak health, asked Alexander to give me this responsibility. He said:

- Kyros has been controlling military provisions and producing weapons for many years. He is a thoughtful worker, so I believe he can complete this job.

Even though I am a slave, because I am close to Leonidas, often visit Mieza, and know Ptolemy, Perdicas, Seleucus, Medius and even Alexander, these people also consider me a friend. The Macedonian army marched through Asia Minor (present-day Türkiye) and camped near the Hellespont port. That afternoon, Alexander suddenly called some friends on a boat to visit the nearby ancient city of Troy. When the boat had not yet completely stopped, Alexander jumped in first, leading the group of people towards the ancient citadel. Standing in front of the ruins of the once famous city of Troy, a place that has entered the poetry, music, and history books of many generations of generations to come, Alexander looked out across the landscape, silently admiring the landscape as if he were immersed in a distant memory, then blurted out:

- The first time the Greeks set foot in Asia was this place - the city of Troy.

I've been here too!

I was surprised when I heard Ptolemy ask:

- When did you come here? How is it possible...

Alexander calmly replied:

- I once crossed the sea with thousands of soldiers on thousands of warships from Greece to Troy, camped on this white sand beach, slept with the soldiers, participated in bloody sieges, and spent many sleepless nights with the generals thinking about how to penetrate the fortified wall to destroy Troy.

Ptolemy, Seleucus and Antigonus looked at each other looked both confused and surprised, but no one said anything. Seeing that everyone didn't seem to believe it, Alexander turned to me and asked loudly:

- Kyros, what do you think? Do you believe that I once came here to participate in the bloodiest battle in Greece to level and burn down Troy?

I was surprised to be asked, not knowing how to answer, but fortunately Timotheus spoke up:

- Dear king, if that's true, where were the giant walls of Troy in the past?

Alexander without thinking, pointed towards the hill:

- Look, you guys. Do you see that hill where there are two big old trees in the distance? The wall of Troy then ran from that hill all the way to the west. A series of solid, majestic and towering city walls stood there, challenging the bravest warriors of Greece. The Greek army thought it could level all the strongholds in this world, but had to watch helplessly as the mighty wall blocked all their attacks for ten long years of hard fighting. Every army attacking Troy was afraid of Hector's army and no one could defeat Prince Hector in one-on-one duels. You should know that I personally killed Hector, the most talented warrior in this place, in a duel to avenge my brother Patroclus, whose sword was stabbed deep into Hector's throat, making me furious. It was dawn, I alone approached the gates of Troy, challenged him to a duel and killed him completely.

There is no longer Hector to command, in the city there is only the army of an old king and Hector's younger brother Paris, a damn prostitute who used seduction tricks and kidnapped the beautiful young woman Helen, who was the wife of the King of Sparta. It was Paris's wrongdoing that led to the disastrous Trojan War. However, even though Prince Hector is dead, we still have no way to take down that fortified gate. I don't know how many bones and blood of Greek warriors fell before this fateful wall...

We were all silent, no one dared to speak or interrupt Alexander because everyone felt that this emperor did not seem to be joking at all. Alexander at that time did not care about us, continued:

- In my life, I have never had the thought of backing down from any enemy. I continued to spend many sleepless nights with the Greek generals thinking of strategies, determined to destroy Troy at all costs. The day we fail to destroy Troy, that day we swear we will never return to our homeland. Finally, Odysseus, king of Ithaca, came up with an unprecedented trick to deceive the king of Troy. We dismantled our warships to use wood to build the most gigantic and magnificent wooden horse in the world and hid inside the horse a group of the best soldiers. After that, we pretended to be sick with a plague, broke camp, boarded ships to withdraw troops, and then placed our troops in a deserted strait nearby. The King of Troy was happy because he thought Greece had finally resigned to defeat and withdrew its troops miserably, leaving on the beach a giant wooden horse as an offering to the gods, meaning a peace offering. Despite warnings from the prophetess Cassandra, King Priam of Troy still decided to let his soldiers drag the wooden horse into the city as a trophy to prove victory. That night, almost all the generals of Troy drank drunkenly to celebrate, lit fires to thank the gods and danced around the wooden horse until late, then fell asleep in alcohol. At that moment, we escaped from the belly of the wooden horse, opened the city gate for the waiting Greek army to rush in, beat the battle-hardened Trojan army to pieces, and then burned and leveled that fortified citadel.

We silently turned to look at each other, half in disbelief, half in disbelief, but Alexander's fiery eyes as he recounted the details of the historic siege made us cold. Alexander didn't care about our half-trusting attitude, but looked toward the end of the horizon and resolutely said:

- I'm back! This time we will conquer Asia, fighting to the end of the world.

No one can stop my steed and this time no one will be able to kill me!

We turned to face the beach. Everyone walked and thought about the upcoming battle with the Persian army, but the story of Troy was stuck in their heads. When approaching the mooring, Alexander turned back to look at the ruins of Troy in the distance for a moment, then suddenly turned to me, his voice low enough for me to hear:

- Kyros! I am Achilles returned.

This unexpected announcement was like a thunderclap in my head. There is no Greek who does not know the myth of the battle of Troy, with famous heroes on both front lines, from Odysseus to Hector, Menelaus, Ajax, Agamemnon and even Achilles. But what about Alexander recognizing himself as Achilles? Extremely surprised, but not daring to be rude, I respectfully asked:

- Dear King! So is it true that Achilles died in the battle of Troy from an arrow shot in his heel?

Alexander silently looked into the distance for a moment and then said:

- The mighty Achilles has never lost a battle. Achilles died because Prince Paris's arrow hit him right in the heel, which was Achilles' only fatal point.

Any hero in this world has a weakness.

Alexander's story raised the question in my mind: Can a person who has been dead for thousands of years return to this world and remember the past, so Alexander could tell in such detail? Is death not the end? Alexander certainly had no reason to lie about this.

He was already a great king, had proven his strategic skills on the battlefield and was famous throughout Greece.

That night, I could hardly sleep because I kept tossing and turning with the question: "Is it true that people can be resurrected in another life? If so, can they retain the personality and understanding from the previous life?". I tried to connect, compare and realize the strange similarities between Emperor Alexander and Achilles - the son of the sea goddess Thetis and the Greek king Peleus in the ancient myths that I had known. It is true that both people have personality and spirit traits that are rare for anyone to have. The story goes that, when he was a child, Achilles was held by his mother, the sea goddess Thetis, by his heel, turned upside down, and dipped his whole body into the water of the Styx River - the river separating earth and the underworld - so that Achilles could have immortality like a god. From then on, Achilles' entire body was as solid as iron and steel, except for the sole of his heel, which was held by the sea goddess with both hands so he could not dip into the sacred water.

Achilles died because of a single weakness in his heel, and did the undefeated Alexander have any weakness? Is there anything that can stop this mighty, undefeated Greek god of war? When will this constant killing end?

In ancient Greece, sages such as Pythagoras, Socrates and Plato were all

The concept that humans have an invisible, immortal soul, different from a visible, mortal body. The concepts of the soul of these sages are more or less different, but in general they still believe that the soul is life, thanks to the soul, the body can live and function. The soul is immortal, when the body dies, the soul moves into another body to continue life. Pythagoras believed that the soul could move into the body of a human or an animal, but Socrates believed that the soul could only move into a human body because the soul is the container of knowledge, while animals do not have knowledge. Therefore, the purpose of human life is to cultivate knowledge to become wiser. Socrates proved the existence of the soul by giving a difficult problem to a group of uneducated slaves to see what they could do. One of those slaves solved the problem, Socrates explained that because this person had studied mathematics in a previous life, the soul remembered the method of solving the problem. This concept of an immortal soul is often criticized and ridiculed by other philosophers.

Platon went further than his teacher (Socrates) by explaining in the book C O ng hoa that humans must go through a necessary journey to learn. The soul has an endless life, while the body has a limit. Therefore, the soul is continuously reincarnated into the body: born, dies, then continues to reincarnate again to learn.

The sins people commit in the first part of the journey will make them pay in the following parts and the things they experience in this life also follow them in the next life. Therefore, Orpheus's soul chose to be reborn as a swan because he did not want to be born as a woman, Thersites was reborn as an orangutan, and Agamemnon as a falcon, Odysseus chose to become a silent ordinary person. If humans can become animals, then animals can be reincarnated into humans. Aggressive animals often become barbarians, gentle animals become polite people, wise animals become intelligent people.

Platon divided the soul into three parts: The rational part (Rational) is located in the brain, the emotional part (Spirited) is located in the heart and the desire part (Appetite) is located in the lower abdomen or genitals. Depending on which part of the person's development, after death, the soul will be reborn into the corresponding body. Souls that develop in theory are often reincarnated into the bodies of kings, leaders, or elites and aristocrats. Emotionally developed souls often move into the bodies of artists, priests or people with artistic talent. Souls that develop sexual desire often move into the bodies of workers, uneducated people or slaves. This concept was somewhat influenced by the class division in society at that time, where people were pushed down to the worker or slave class without any knowledge or understanding.

The Greeks believed that when people do great and great things, after death, they become gods, living in the realm of the gods. However, gods are not much different from humans. Even though they are gods, they are also greedy, selfish, like eating, drinking, drinking, arguing and lustful like humans, the only difference is that they have power so they can do things that humans cannot do.

Part Eight

PERSIA: CONQUEST AND LOVE

The war between Greece and Persia began with a battle on the banks of the Granicus River. At that time, the Persian army had gathered its forces, gathering rebels from Athens to join forces to fight Alexander, so the military strength of both sides was clearly different. When setting up the battle, General Parmenion studied and observed the situation on both sides and then asked Alexander to maintain his position, waiting for the Persian army to attack first. Alexander shook his head and asserted:

- No, the best defense is to attack. Must attack first by surprise.

If you play first, you can win.

That night, military orders were sent down to the entire army to get ready for war.

At the beginning of the battle, the Greek army was supported by brass, war drums and majestic music to help the army burn with enthusiasm, the soldiers were filled with enthusiasm as if they were participating in a great holy war and dying under the flag of Alexander's army was a sacred honor, there was nothing to regret.

In a war where one side is an army that is not afraid of death, the fear is often on the other side. Unlike normal commanders, who only stay behind to give orders, Alexander wore armor, rode a horse, drew his sword, and led the assault troops, moving forward. This is a rare risky action, because generals with extensive battlefield experience usually never do this. As soon as they saw Alexander galloping forward, the Persian generals immediately aimed at Alexander, because if they killed the king, it would be like a sheep. The young king was immediately surrounded by four Persian generals but he did not appear to flinch in the slightest. Alexander fought bravely, stabbing two Persian generals to death but was also hit in the head with a spear. Luckily, thanks to the thick helmet, the king was only slightly concussed. When Alexander's sword was broken, there was no weapon left in his hand and was fiercely attacked by a Persian general, fortunately Cleitus risked his life to rush in to assist. Cleitus cut off the other general's arm, then immediately gave his sword to Alexander. Having his weapon back, Alexander continued to attack. Seeing the king's bravery and risking his life, the entire Greek army fought wholeheartedly, breaking the chains in the Persian posture. Faced with the momentum and suicidal spirit of the Greek army, the Persian commander eventually had to order his soldiers to retreat. The Persian army suffered heavy losses, the Greek side suffered few casualties and won. In addition to capturing many weapons, they also captured many prisoners. Alexander ordered all those who betrayed the Greek army and joined the Persian army to be prosecuted. The emperor then ordered:

- Let's make it clear to everyone everywhere that any Greek who betrays the country must suffer the same fate as these traitors.

Although I did not directly participate in the battle, I witnessed this brutal execution with my own eyes and could not help but be horrified. Screams and pleas echoed throughout the barracks. Looking at the Athenian soldiers dying under the swords of the Macedonian soldiers, my heart was filled with a strange feeling of pity like when I witnessed the massacre at Thebes. The former commander of the Athenian army, Memnon, the leader of the rebel force, ran away with the Persian generals, and the soldiers under him, just because they were loyal to their commander's orders, are now bleeding.

After the victory at Granicus, Alexander pulled his army to the South, attacking along the coast to capture the ports, preventing Persia from attacking Greece by sea. Before each battle, Alexander and his soldiers sang majestic songs together, accompanied by the sounds of war drums and bronze trumpets, shielding the Persian army, most of whom were local soldiers, in fear of the fierceness of the Greek army. In just a short time, ports such as Miletus and Halicarnassus all fell.

From then on, Greece controlled the coastal region of Asia Minor, cutting off all maritime transport routes of the Persian navy. Alexander ordered Ptolemy to bring a fleet of warships to massively attack the Greek islands that had been occupied by Persia.

The Persian troops stationed on those islands all surrendered. Since then, the Mediterranean was liberated, Greek fishing boats were free to go to sea, without fear.

The Granicus victory created a great buzz throughout Greece and the surrounding countries. This is the first time the Greek people have tasted victory after many years of living in worry and fear. Greek soldiers who died in battle were carefully buried in accordance with the proper rituals, their families also received death benefits and were exempted from paying taxes for three years. Seeing that Greek soldiers were well treated and had high salaries, many young people from surrounding countries also volunteered to join the expeditionary force. Thanks to these mercenaries, the number of Greek troops increased significantly, but it also depleted the royal treasury, making me start to worry, wondering if the war dragged on, where would the money come from to pay for the war? I'm afraid the slave trade will happen again.

Alexander marched his army through Lydia, Ionia, Armenia and surrounding areas, all without encountering any significant resistance. Local generals could not resist the well-trained elite Greek army. In just over half a year, the Greek army took control of Asia Minor, a large, rich land with enough food to sustain the army through the winter of that year. Since the Mediterranean has been liberated, I can travel back to Pella by boat, which is faster than traveling on land. I continued to be the messenger for Leonidas and Melissa, and also listened to the love songs the two composed for each other.

When arriving at the localities, Alexander ordered Timotheus to collect books and documents and send them back for Aristotle to study. As the person in charge of military provisions, often traveling between Pella and military positions, I was ordered to bring these collected documents back to Mieza. Thanks to that, I met Timotheus often, and over time our friendship became closer. Luckily, in the midst of chaos and chaos, with blood spilling everywhere, I had an intelligent and knowledgeable friend to confide in. During a conversation, when we were both drunk, I accidentally let out a complaint:

- Why are some people born happy while others have to be slaves?

I don't understand why there is such class distinction?

Timotheus replied with a slightly slurred voice because he was tipsy:

- When born, people are different. Smart people who can reason and have high knowledge should be in charge. People who are incapable and only know how to obey orders are slaves. Slaves are necessary for society because this force ensures the operation of a previously established social order. This is a reasonable arrangement, without which society would become chaotic. Thanks to the master, the slaves were fed and housed, so they had to obey and do what the master wanted. This is a win-win situation and the slaves have to depend on the slave owner because they do not have the ability to think independently.

Of course I do not accept this way of speaking, but not wanting to tense up with my friend, I gently objected:

- But who has the right to decide who has the ability and who does not? How do we know that this newborn baby is smarter than that baby?

Timotheus did not flinch and answered decisively:

- Ancient laws clearly stated that if parents are slaves, then their children must also be slaves. Slaves who were not capable of independent thinking could not give birth to intelligent children. Intelligence ability depends on family bloodline.

I couldn't accept this explanation, so I immediately reacted:

- Having said that, during the war, the losing side had many people forced into slavery. Even though they were not originally slaves, they were also smart and educated, and their children also had to be slaves. How to explain the issue of intelligence by blood?

Timotheus paused, thought for a moment, then nodded and said:

- Kyros, what you say makes sense. This is something we have never thought of before. The division of slave classes has been a tradition, existing for a long time, it is unknown when, and it is unknown who created this division. Just like our teachers, Plato and Aristotle, taught us that. Right now I can't answer your question, but eventually I will find the answer.

Even though the conversation happened while we were both drunk and I didn't mention it again after that, I didn't expect this question to make Timotheus think a lot later.

Living near the young king and the scholars who accompanied him, I gradually realized that Alexander was not only a talented commander on the battlefield but also an emperor with an extremely simple lifestyle. On the battlefield, he lived in a tent just like the soldiers. Every morning, he got up early and randomly chose a team of soldiers to practice with. Activities can be very diverse, from practicing sports, practicing martial arts, to archery, javelin throwing, sword fighting; After training, he will eat and drink with his soldiers, there is absolutely no difference between an emperor and ordinary soldiers. After each battle, the king went to console, inquire about the soldiers' injuries and did not hesitate to show them the wounds on his own body, so he was deeply admired by the soldiers. In the dark, the young king still wandered around the camp, drinking and singing with the soldiers. Accompanying him were a group of close friends such as Perdicas, Hephaestion, Ptolemy, Antigonus, who had played with him since childhood. Because they studied together and grew up together, they also liked singing and drinking like Alexander. In addition, every day Alexander spent time learning more with Greek scholars or discussing with them about running the places he had just conquered. Alexander was a wise strategist. Wherever he went, he had people survey the terrain first to choose a place to station troops and drew a map of the area with careful details of rivers, hills, and roads.

As for the Persian court, initially, when it heard of the Greek attack, the court still thought that the local generals were strong enough to cope, so they did not send reinforcements. When large lands and important islands were lost, Persian King Darius III summoned his generals and personally brought troops to deal with them. He advocated blocking Alexander's retreat from Asia Minor to Greece to destroy the Greek army right on his own land. With hundreds of chariots, thousands of skilled cavalry and three times more soldiers than the Greek army, Darius believed he had victory in his hands.

Hearing that King Darius personally brought troops to station in Damascus, Alexander gathered his generals and looked at the terrain map to prepare for the response. Hearing reports of the overwhelming number of Persian troops and chariots, Parmenion was cautious:

- Persia is famous for its strategy of using chariots to break the enemy front, followed by a large infantry force, which can use the advantage of numbers to sweep and win...

Alexander interrupted:

- Don't worry, I have studied Persia's strategy and know how to deal with it. Darius is a king but has never led an army into battle, so why should we be afraid of a pack of lions led by a lamb.

After studying the terrain, instead of forming a battle formation on the vast plain, Alexander ordered the army to withdraw to Issus Pass to wait for the Persian army to arrive. This is a narrow terrain, with mountains on one side and the sea on the other. There are many undulating and jagged rocks around, so when entering battle, Persian chariots cannot run fast but have to circle around to avoid the rocks. Because of the rugged terrain, some chariots tripped over rocks and overturned, not only losing their ability to fight but also hindering other chariots, so from the beginning, Persia lost the advantage of attacking with chariots. Following the chariot was a group of cavalry and infantry who charged forward to attack. Greek soldiers used very long spears, divided into Phalanx* formations to maintain position, while Persian soldiers used short weapons such as swords and swords to attack in a mass-based marching style, so they were at a disadvantage when dealing with long spears. Greek soldiers were protected by solid armor, standing behind shields, using six-meter-long sarissa spears, moving step by step to the majestic sound of war drums. The elite Persian cavalry, considered the terror of all battlefields throughout Asia Minor and Mesopotamia, could not overcome the barrier of specially long spears used to deal with this cavalry. Encountering a solidly disciplined line, only advancing step by step to the beat of the Greeks' war drums, one person fell and was immediately replaced by another. The rows and layers were like iron fences with long sharp spears, so the Persian army, even though it was large and skilled, soon broke up and was overwhelmed in spirit.

Yasamin is Leonidas's new wife. I was so surprised by Melissa's strangely calm attitude. Why is she not angry or hateful towards the person who betrayed her?

Why does she still want to send gifts to the child of the woman who stole her husband? I remember when the two of them first fell in love, Leonidas wrote:

"Aristotle taught that for everything, it is necessary to ask the question "Why" to find out the root cause, because everything in this world is arranged according to logic that can be explained", so how to explain this strange, "illogical" thing?

Even though he became emperor of the world's largest empire, Alexander was still interested in the uprisings demanding independence in Greece that Antipater had to work to suppress. To maintain security, Antipater issued many strict laws and acted like an emperor, thus displeasing Queen Olympias. She sent a letter to Alexander complaining about this general's autocracy. That's why Alexander called Antipater to meet him immediately.

After reading the letter, Antipater knew that if he wasn't careful, he could be killed like Philotas and Parmenion, so he used the excuse of being busy and sent his son Cassander to meet Alexander on his behalf. Cassander was the husband of Thessalonike, Alexander's sister, so he could avoid the emperor's wrath.

That day Cassander entered the court and was surprised to see that Alexander was not wearing Greek clothes but had changed to wearing Persian clothes. The king sat on the throne while the mandarins and generals all knelt on the ground. Persian customs clearly state that in the court, officials must kneel and bow to the ground, only when called can they raise their heads (Proskynesis ritual). This is unacceptable to the Greeks.

Seeing the scene of the mandarins crawling on the ground like that, Cassander was surprised and then burst out laughing. This attitude made Alexander furious. The king rushed over and grabbed Cassander, repeatedly smashing his head against the wall, blood pouring out.

The young king shouted:

- Why didn't Antipater come and let a brat come and cause chaos in my court? If I don't respect Thessalonike, I will kill him today.

When reviewing the treasury accounts at Pella presented by Dimitris, Alexander ordered the documents in Babylon to be compared and found that a large amount of gold had been lost. The king was angry:

- Why is there this deviation? Kyros has inventoried everything here and recorded it clearly. Why are Pella's books different?

Philiteus, the commander of the soldiers escorting the gold, was called.

Philiteus confirmed that the seals in the gold barrels were intact when they arrived at Pella and were also confirmed by Dimitris before opening the seals, so Alexander ordered Harpalus to personally return to Pella to investigate.

***

Although he conquered many places and was honored as the King of a Asia, to the people

From Persia, Alexander was still a foreigner. To be accepted by the people, Alexander needed to become close to the royal family of this country. Therefore, the king asked to marry Barsine, commonly known as Stateira (Stateira II), the eldest daughter of King Darius.

After that, he also asked to marry Parysatis, the youngest daughter of King Ochus*.

Through two marriages and being the son-in-law of two former emperors, Alexander officially became a member of the Achaemenid family, a family that had ruled Persia for more than two hundred years. The Achaemenid family has ruled Persia for many generations, and members of this family all hold important positions, so as a member of this family, Alexander is not afraid of betrayal. Alexander's trusted friends, such as Hephaestion, Simonides, and before that, Seleucus, also married people of the Persian noble family.

(*) King Artaxerxes III Ochus, ruler of Ba T in 359 in 338 BC.

From then on, the court of the Greek Empire in Babylon began to change to a new, harmonious tone, with officers and generals consisting of both ethnicities. It's nice on the outside, but inside the harem it's different. When Alexander had two new wives, Roxana's status became inferior. She is just the daughter of the border chief of Bactria, and cannot be compared to the two royal princesses of the previous dynasty. As a heroic emperor, he defeated the East and conquered the North, conquered the battlefield and ruled the largest empire in the world at that time, but Alexander could not resolve the quarrels and jealousy between his wives. Therefore, he often tried to hide himself and monitor and check on soldiers everywhere so that he could freely sing and drink with the soldiers. However, the emperor could not hide forever. He still had to return to the court to manage court affairs and often had to resolve disputes, quarrels, and jealousy between his three wives. Stateira and Parysatis are both princesses, knowing the etiquette and rules of the royal bedroom, while Roxana, although she is a noble child, grew up on the border, has a strong and indomitable personality, and is not suitable for the rules of the palace. In the end, Alexander had to take Roxana to his private palace in Susa and leave the other two wives in Babylon.

***

One day, Alexander called Cleitus to court and appointed this general as general

Governor of Bactria. Among Alexander's close friends, Cleitus was the one who followed King Philip to quell the rebellion, accomplished many achievements, and trained infantry in the Phalanx formation, so he was very popular with the soldiers. During the expedition, Cleitus always followed Alexander in every battle and once saved the king's life in the battle of Granicus.

Not wanting to bother with court rituals as well as avoid having to deal with wives or complaints in the harem, Alexander took the opportunity to send Cleitus on his way, so he invited his friends to go to the camp away from Babylon, held a celebration party, and sang together like in the past. It's been a long time since we've been able to drink freely, so at the party everyone drank until they forgot the world. Wine flows in and out, all the things stored in the hearts of the generals and soldiers flow out with the alcohol. Although he was appointed governor, Cleitus believed that being a general without being able to command the army or participate in battle, being sent to be a ruler in a remote place was a sign of falling from grace. While drunk, Cleitus complained that with his life and death efforts, it was unfair to only be governor in a wild border region, where tribes often rebelled, with a few thousand old and weak soldiers. Alexander was also drunk at that time, so he shouted:

- I have conquered Bactria and crushed the rebels. There's nothing left for people to worry about. You were lucky because you were able to get the governorship thanks to me. If you had remained in Pella, you would have been just a lowly soldier, but there was no way you could reach this position.

Cleitus was also led by alcohol at that time, arguing loudly:

- If it weren't for the Phalanx squad trained by me, how could you win against the Persian army. As a Macedonian, he dared to wear Persian clothes, marry a Persian wife, behave like a Persian, so shameless...

Alexander got angry, threw the bottle of wine he was drinking in Cleitus's face and called the soldiers to arrest Cleitus for immediate execution, but everyone quickly stopped him. All the generals at that party were close friends, had played together since childhood, had gone through many battles together, so no one wanted things to go further. Alexander called for someone to bring weapons so he could punish the impudent man. Perdicas and Philiteus hurriedly pulled Cleitus out of the tent, but Alexander immediately chased after him, grabbed the spear of a nearby guard, and rushed straight into Cleitus. During the struggle, Cleitus just turned around and the spear pierced his chest.

The death of Cleitus caused great confusion in the Macedonian army. Although Alexander was very remorseful when he sobered up, gave him a proper burial, and ordered a large amount of gold to be brought back to Cleitus's family, the soldiers, especially the Phalanx army, who were loyal to their commander, were extremely dissatisfied. For a long time, Macedonian soldiers did not accept that their emperor changed court rituals, dressed like Persians, and forced mandarins to kneel when entering court. Discontent spread further when Alexander appointed Philiteus to command the Phalanx squad in place of Cleitus, and some soldiers rebelled. A fight broke out among Macedonian soldiers. Thanks to the trusted guards of Perdicas and Hephaestion, these soldiers were eventually captured.

However, during the fight, Leonidas was seriously injured. Hearing the news, I immediately went to the infirmary and saw my old friend lying there with blood all over his body. Seeing me, Leonidas whispered:

- I know it's difficult for me to continue living, I hope you think of our old friendship and do me a favor.

I put my hand on Leonidas's forehead:

- Just say it, I will try my best.

Leonidas whispered:

- I'm worried about Yasamin... She's about to give birth, she can't live in a chaotic place like this. Alexander is preparing to march to conquer new kingdoms. If the Greek army leaves this place, I don't feel safe letting Yasamin stay here. Can you take my wife back to Greece and protect her?

This is a heavy responsibility, moreover, the incident was so unexpected, it made me somewhat hesitant. However, seeing Leonidas' bloody body, I didn't want my close friend to worry before closing his eyes, so I reluctantly nodded.

Leonidas happily held my hand tightly, weakly saying thank you. The next day, Leonidas died. After burying my friend, I went to find Yasamin to talk about Leonidas's proposal, but she refused, determined not to leave Babylon.

Leonidas's death and the rebellion of the Greek soldiers made Alexander extremely angry. He ordered Perdicas to control the army more strictly and demobilized some Greek soldiers, letting them return to their homeland.

With the troops recruited from the places that surrendered to his hooves, he did not need many Greek soldiers anymore.

When I returned to Pella, I informed Dimitris of his son's death but said nothing about Leonidas' commission. Dimitris was extremely miserable, all the hopes he had placed on his only son were dashed. Sophia, the daughter he arranged to marry Philotas, is now also a widow. The Parmenion family's assets were also confiscated. Too sad, Dimitris sent a letter to Antipater asking to resign and hand over everything to Deasius, Isidora's husband.

Before I left to return to Persia, Melissa came to see me, looking more haggard than before, she asked:

- I know that Leonidas was carefully buried by Emperor Alexander. But how is Yasamin? Who will take care of Leonidas' child?

Once again, Melissa's calm attitude and saintly soul surprised me. Obviously, Leonidas's death was a huge pain for her, but why did she still care about that woman right now? I had to tell Melissa Leonidas' last words and Yasamin's refusal to leave Babylon.

Melissa immediately said:

- You promised to help Leonidas, so why don't you bring her back here?

I answered:

- Yasamin did not want to leave Babylon. I can't force her.

Melissa was silent for a moment then said:

- I have lived alone for many years, so I understand what lonely people feel like. Yasamin cannot live in that chaotic place without anyone to protect her, please try to bring her back here.

I was so surprised, I asked:

- But... wasn't she the one who stole your husband?

Melissa said leisurely:

- Leonidas wants to bring Yasamin to live here, so do I. You yourself promised Leonidas the same thing. Furthermore, I also have to worry about Leonidas' child. It cannot live in such an insecure, chaotic place.

When I returned to Babylon, Yasamin had given birth to a baby girl. I tried to persuade her, but she refused to leave. I discussed the matter with Antigenidas. He thought for a moment and then said:

- If Yasamin doesn't want to go then that's it. But Leonidas' child is different. Even though it is Leonidas's child with another woman, it is still technically my grandchild.

I can't let him live alone here, you bring the baby back here, I can find a woman who has just given birth to take care of the baby among the slaves.

I don't have the heart to do that, so I found a way to avoid it. But Antigenidas was determined.

Because I still have to distribute salaries to soldiers in different places, I am not present in Babylon often. But on the way back to Greece, to the port of Issus, I learned that Antigenidas had sent someone to capture Leonidas' child and sent a slave to look after it and hand it over to Melissa. The next time we met, we had a fierce argument about this. Finally, Antigenidas got angry:

- You are just a slave while I command the soldiers and have full power in my hands.

What I want to do is my business, you have no right to object. If it weren't for the friendship between us, this sword would have been stuck in your chest.

That statement severely damaged our friendship. From then on I avoided meeting Antigenidas again. Because Leonidas had passed away and there was no more correspondence, I did not return to Pella but tried to stay permanently in Athens. I learned that Melissa became the mother taking care of Leonidas's months-old child.

***

In my conversation with Thomas, he said these days it's almost all

The documents about Alexander were all written by ancient Greeks, so there are many prejudices.

Most praised Alexander as a great hero and considered the conquest of Persia a victory of Europeans over Asian countries. Most historical documents often promote Greek civilization and consider Persia a barbaric, cruel, backward and uncivilized land. This also influenced later centuries when European countries considered themselves the civilizational center of the world and looked down on other civilizations. When they invaded Asian and African countries, they called this war the liberation of uncivilized peoples.

Thomas said that although Greek civilization had advanced very highly with the presence of philosophers such as Pythagoras, Plato, Socrates, Aristotle... the Persian Empire at that time had also developed very strongly in economics, agriculture and trade. While Greece was still a collection of small city-states, the Persian Empire expanded everywhere, stretching from Egypt to India. Since ancient times, Persians have traveled everywhere to trade, through the Silk Road, all the way to China.

Persian literature, poetry, and music also reached an important position and were popular throughout the Middle East, so it cannot be concluded that the Persian Empire was uncivilized.

Another fact shows that at that time Greek law was only limited to class division and land ownership for tax collection. Other matters are decided by the royal court, in which the king has absolute authority. Meanwhile, Persia had a rule of law system with clearly recorded laws, not centralized authority in individual kings. Persian religion (Zorism) clearly distinguishes the concepts of good, evil, right and wrong. The Avesta Sutra opens with the sentence: “Think think go about u thi en, say about u thi yen, do thou thi yen because Ii act swill be judged by Ahura Mazda." The principle of not lying and always speaking the truth was clearly written into the law of King Cyrus. Zoroastrianism divides things very clearly, does not accept slavery, does not discriminate against other religions such as Judaism or the religions of Egypt and Assyria.

Most historians write that Alexander was engrossed in conquering the world, did not return to Greece and died early, so his dream was not fulfilled. Thomas made it clear to me that Alexander had no intention of returning to Greece. He had established a new court in Babylon to rule the vast empire he had conquered, so there was no need to return to Pella. That is why Alexander ordered the treasury to be transferred to Persia, developing a new generation of citizens, blending the Greek and Persian bloodlines for this empire. He married Stateira, daughter of King Darius and married Parysatis daughter of King Ochus, which is evidence of his desire to become friends with the people of this country. Instead of using Greeks in government affairs, he still let Mazaeus be the minister, and Persian mandarins ran everything in the country.

Today, archaeologists have found gold coins minted in Babylon at that time, with two sides, one side printed with Alexander's image, the other side printed with Mazaeus's image as historical proof of the merger of two bloodlines, these two civilizations into one. This is a fact of Greek history that some historians probably do not want to mention.

Thomas told me that Alexander the Great's great dream of unifying the world seemed to be the most unrealistic and extravagant thing a person could think of. How can we make people in the world no longer have distance, no longer have enmity, and live together peacefully? If this world no longer has gaps in ethnicity, skin color, religion, and politics, will humans end division, hatred, invasion, and killing each other? Is there a miracle that can make people in all countries consider each other as people of the same country and will war, killing, and violence end forever on this planet? Isn't it true that when we escape the atmosphere, enter the vast universe and look at planet Earth, we can deeply feel how small we are in this universe and that we all share the same homeland?

Is there a miracle that can make humans stop destroying the lives of all species, stop destroying the green color on this earth's homeland? Is there any way to prevent this planet from counting down to the end of the world? Is what has been happening in this world the wrath of the Creator or simply cyclical retributions according to the law of Cause and Effect of the universe?

If we are in the final stage of the cycle of Thanh - Tr dd - Ho, i - Di ê t, is there any way to stop that destruction, when we ourselves are the cause of all destruction? The most terrible destruction to the life and future of all species?

Those questions keep spinning in my mind when thinking about Alexander and his endless wars. Humans have always dreamed and aimed for a peaceful world, but until today, when humanity is proud of its civilization and its peak scientific and technological development, this planet has not stopped conflicts and upheavals.

If people only pursue competition and power struggles to dominate each other, is what we call civilization really worthy of being a civilization?

Part nine

INDIA: POWER AND AWAKENING

After ten years of war, Alexander became the emperor of the most powerful empire in the world at that time. Just as he told me: "Achilles never lost a battle" and neither did you. Through hundreds of battles, large and small, he became a king who won every battle on the battlefield. Even when facing an enemy force many times larger, he was still able to win. He won not only because he knew how to use sharp and ingenious strategies but also because of his steadfast will and courageous spirit, not afraid of any enemy. In every battle, Alexander bravely charged forward, general fighting general, despite the barrage of arrows and spears, inspiring all soldiers to fight the enemy decisively. Therefore, his body was covered with scars left by enemy swords and spears. When training with soldiers, he did not hesitate to strip naked to show them the scars on his body. This made the soldiers admire him even more and wholeheartedly follow him to fight.

Not long after Cassander's arrival in Babylon, Alexander received a dispatch from Harpalus reporting that the treasury at Pella only had about 1,500 talents of gold in reserve, and if it did not find more gold, it would be difficult for the court to maintain such a large army. This made Alexander extremely angry because he suspected there had been fraud in the management of the Pella royal treasury, but the culprit was unknown. He knew that after the deaths of Philotas and Parmenion and the humiliation of Cassander, it would be difficult to call Antipater to Babylon for questioning. He was also concerned that if handled too harshly, it could cause division or rebellion in his own homeland. Therefore, he discussed with Timotheus about discharging some soldiers to cut costs. Timotheus offered to collect taxes from the conquered lands, but Alexander hesitated because he had previously promised local governors to keep the taxes. Currently, your empire has just been established and is not yet completely stable. You do not want to make changes that could lead to chaos.

While the king still could not find a solution, a few days later Mazaeus brought a Persian merchant to court. This person said that their trading delegations often followed the trail across the Hindu Kush range to exchange goods with the kingdoms located east of the mountains, which were very rich kingdoms, rich land, prosperous residents with a lot of gold, silver and jewels. Alexander was extremely surprised by what he had just heard, because all previous documents recorded that the Hindu Kush range was the end of the world. Even King Cyrus only conquered Bactria, the country near the Hindu Kush and stopped his army there, not going further. If that mountain range is indeed not the end of the world and on the other side are new lands, then you must definitely explore. Alexander immediately ordered people to accompany the merchant group to follow that road to research and draw detailed maps. From then on, he constantly thought about a new conquest. He told Timotheus:

- If Bactria and the Hindu Kush range are not the end of the world, then we must go to the end to explore and expand the borders of our empire.

A few months later, Alexander received a complete report on the trail (today's Khyber Pass ) along with a detailed map of how to cross this mountain range.

Alexander immediately prepared his army for a new expedition. He summoned a number of generals such as Ptolemy and Antigonus to bring troops to join the expeditionary army and appointed Perdicas as deputy commander of the army, Hephaestion as commander of the cavalry. He also ordered Philiteus and I to return to Pella to transfer the gold and silver in the treasury to Babylon. He said to me:

- Kyros, you just take care of minting enough money. When we conquer those kingdoms, we will bring back a lot of gold.

This official trip back to Greece no longer makes me as enthusiastic as before.

Thinking about the long expedition in those distant places, I can't help but worry and wonder when this constant fighting will end? I thought of Philotas and his question: "If the war continues like this, when will we be able to return to Greece?" Indeed, I see that many Macedonian soldiers are tired of this long-lasting war. Has the ambition to dominate the world overshadowed the young king's original purpose? Did the spirit of victory cause Alexander to become arrogant and complacent, leading to the deaths of Philotas and Parmenion? Was it just because he did not accept the mixing of Greek and Persian cultures that Cleitus was killed? I sadly think about the fate of those who were both friends and loyal servants of Alexander.

No matter how many glorious victories they had, it seemed that they were not enough to satisfy the Great Emperor's ambition. Perhaps, when power reaches a certain level, anyone can become domineering, greedy and never know enough. Once again, I heard in my head what the poet Homer said in the epic Iliad, no one goes through war and remains the same.

At that time, I could only feel sorry for those who had been worn down by war, even taking their lives, without knowing that this time disaster would strike me.

When I first arrived in Athens, I was suddenly arrested because someone accused me of embezzling funds. The person who denounced was Deasius, Isidora's husband, who was currently taking care of the royal treasury on behalf of Dimitris. I only know that the treasury is missing some gold, this has been reported to Emperor Alexander but why should I be the one accused? He often compliments me on my thoughtful work and believes in my ability to calculate accurately, so why did this incident happen today?
