- For many years, all the transport of gold from Persia to Pella has been under the care of Kyros. The spending and collection of gold and silver to mint coins for military food is also under my own control, and the books for the treasury are also done by him. Currently, the treasury lacks a significant amount of gold. Up until now, he was the only one who looked after and controlled everything. If he wasn't the culprit, who else would come in here?

Too unjustly, I spoke up to defend:

- All revenue and expenditure are recorded in books. The gold crates transported from Persia were all carefully sealed. When he arrived at Pella, Mr. Dimitris himself checked and confirmed it before transferring it to the treasury. The minting of coins and weapons, all go through you...

Deasius shouted loudly to interrupt me:

- You can't blame anyone. All expenditures and revenues are inspected and supervised by people. Dimitris treated him so kindly that he took advantage of his kindness for his own gain. This crime must be severely punished.

Harpalus also spoke up:

- I have looked at all the shipping records and revenue and expenditure records but found that there are many unclear places, some numbers have been altered. There was definitely something shady going on. Wherever you hide your gold, you must reveal it immediately, otherwise don't blame us too harshly.

I immediately objected:

- How could such a thing happen? Up to now, the books have always been transparent. Every time Mr. Dimitris looked carefully and was satisfied. I have been doing this for more than ten years, without any mistakes. There's nothing shady going on. If you don't believe me, just ask Mr. Dimitris, he is the one in control and in charge...

Deasius chuckled:

- You are very good, but you still blame the dead.

What did Deasius just say? Dimitris passed away? I couldn't believe my ears and stammered back:

- What... Mr. Dimitris... passed away?

Suddenly, from the crowd, Isidora stepped out and pointed straight at me:

- Kyros, you damn slave! You are just a lowly slave, but my father has treated you so kindly. My father not only raised and taught him but also trusted him with important responsibilities. Unexpectedly, the person who did something wrong, stole the gold, would blame my father, a dead man, unable to justify it. My father's kindness was mistakenly placed on an ungrateful person like you.

Isidora cried and talked, exposing my status as a slave. People around me began to whisper and curse me severely. Isidora's sudden accusation caused me great pain, my throat was choked, I couldn't say anything. Every sentence she said was like a sword stabbing into my heart, causing sharp pain. I didn't expect that the person I secretly loved for so many years could say such harsh words. I bowed my head in shame because the words "slave" and "ungrateful person" caused me so much pain. I'm also so shocked that Dimitris passed away. I know that the death of Leonidas, his only son, made him miserable and sick, but his passing was a shock to me.

I looked up at Isidora and wanted to speak but couldn't say a word.

Isidora stepped forward and spat straight into my face, snarling:

- That damn slave, I didn't expect you could be so vile and cruel.

Dare to blame the person who raised you... Go and die!

After speaking, Isidora turned around and sobbed as she walked, making everyone around her feel sorry for her and even more dissatisfied with the sinner, me. Parliament President Desmothenes stepped out:

- Kyros, do you have anything else to say?

I was still stunned by Isidora's sudden insult so I couldn't say anything. Seeing my silence, Demosthenes smiled faintly, then in the eloquent voice of someone used to speaking in front of crowds, he made strong arguments about the fact that I was the only person who controlled the gold and silver in the treasury as well as the revenue and expenditure books, then asked the question, besides me, who knows how much or how little gold is in the warehouse? Over the years, no one knew how much the budget had been lost. It was only when Harpalus investigated that he discovered the shortage... I was the only one who knew exactly how much gold was collected and spent, I was the only one who brought gold to mint coins, then I was the one who brought money to distribute salaries to the soldiers, everything was excess or lacking, only I knew. Only I can do the deficit and amend the entire revenue and expenditure books, no one else can do it. Finally, Demosthenes concluded that I was the culprit. He added that even though I was tortured, I still did not tell him where I hid the gold, so he recommended a death sentence. The entire council raised their hands to vote in agreement. Demosthenes ordered the sentence to be executed immediately to set an example for the people. Even though I was confused about the unexpected turn of events, Dimitris's death and Isidora's harsh words, I was still calm and indignant at such a hasty verdict. I stood up and was about to protest, but fortunately, Philiteus stepped out:

- Wait, this must be decided by Emperor Alexander. His crime will be recorded, but the order must be decided by the king himself.

Demosthenes shook his head:

- At this time, Emperor Alexander is busy far away. Here everything is decided by the parliament. We have voted, we must implement it immediately.

Philiteus angrily shouted:

- Athens is not the royal court. If desired, Kyros must be brought back to Pella for Antipater to be tried. He is a member of the military and must be tried according to military law. Your civil parliament has no right in this matter.

Philiteus's bold statement startled everyone in the parliament.

Seeing that the parliament seemed to flinch, Harpalus spoke up:

- I have been entrusted by the Emperor to handle this matter. I have investigated and compared the records between Babylon and Pella and found where the leak was. I have absolutely the right to execute this order.

Philiteus looked intently at Harpalus and then chuckled:

- But I am also responsible for this matter. If Kyros is guilty, then I have the right to decide. I propose to bring Kyros back to Pella to be tried by Antipater.

The fate of the Macedonians cannot be left to Athens to decide. I do not accept that.

Philiteus's statement touches on something sensitive in the relationship between the two regions.

From ancient times until now, the people of Athens and Macedonia still do not like each other. The young Macedonian king's work to unify Greece made the Athenians dissatisfied. Therefore, although the parliament had its power limited by the royal court, the Athenians still tried to maintain autonomy by continuing to meet in parliament to run everything. However, bringing a Macedonian, who was also under Alexander's command, to trial and sentence him to death could lead to serious consequences. No one knows what this Great Emperor who conquered the North and South will do, because the example of burning Thebes and forcing people to sell into slavery is still imprinted in the minds of the people and parliament of Athens. Although Harpalus was assigned to investigate this matter, he was only an administrative officer, while Philiteus was the commander of the army, and could apply pressure if the parliament did not obey orders. Thanks to Philiteus's intervention, the trial was postponed and I was taken back to Pella.

On the way, Philiteus came to see me privately, he said:

- I see something wrong with this. Why were they so quick to blame and condemn him? There must be some sinister reason. I will immediately report to Alexander so he can intervene in this matter.

Even though he was the regent governing Greece and had his headquarters in Athens, Antipater was busy dealing with the uprising demanding independence from the surrounding small states so he was not often present here. Even at Pella, he and Queen Mother Olympias did not like each other, so he often avoided them, leaving everything to the court officials to take care of. These people are forever intoxicated with the spirit of victory, only knowing how to party, have fun, and enjoy the spoils brought home such as gold, silver, wine, meat, and women, so no one pays attention to court affairs anymore. The Pella court pushed responsibility to the Athens parliament and Athens pushed responsibility to the Babylonian court, so everything was stagnant, no one wanted to make any decisions without Alexander being present.

When Philiteus left Pella to return to Persia, I thought my case could be resolved within a few months. However, the Pella court decided to let Alexander judge, while the king was busy fighting constantly, so my imprisonment gradually fell into oblivion. I lived in prison at Pella for more than two years without hearing any more news. My time here was a long series of extremely bitter days, although I was not beaten or treated as cruelly as in Athens.

This was also the time I thought more about my slave status. For many years, when I was in charge of royal duties, no one knew anything about my background. Billionaire Farnum comes from a family of immigrants from Lebanon. Despite his father's hardships, Farnum was always an excellent student and received a scholarship to college. Like most classes here, students must work in groups on research projects initiated by professors. Each group must carefully research and defend their project in front of the class. Farnum was elected by the group to present and defend the project in front of the class. Law classes often feature fierce debates and the speaker is responsible for defending the group's research. In every debate, Famum rarely loses. He presented concisely, clearly, and with sharp arguments, earning praise from professors and admiration from students in class. After graduating, we each went our separate ways. I worked in New York, Farnum built his career in Chicago. Since then, we have no longer contacted each other. Much later, when Farnum became famous as one of the most successful billionaires because of his early investments in technology companies Microsoft, Apple, Google, Amazon, Facebook, I heard much about him.

Until one day, I received a phone call from Farnum's personal lawyer, saying that Farnum wanted to meet with me to discuss handing over his financial investment fund to my company to manage. This request was quite surprising to me, because we had not been in touch for many years. I asked the other lawyer directly:

- I know Chicago has many famous financial companies. Why did you choose my company?

The lawyer smiled and replied:

- I also gave a list of many reputable companies there, but my client definitely wants to entrust this important job to you. I think maybe because the two of you have known each other before.

I was a bit surprised, so I answered:

- It's true that I know Famum. We knew each other when we were students. But we only studied together in one law course, and after that we didn't have any interaction. For decades, we haven't had any contact with each other.

The other end of the line was surprised:

- That's really strange, I thought you two must have known each other for a long time.

After the lawyer carefully presented the details of the contract, I became even more cautious. Even for an investment company of my size, an investment fund of more than eight hundred million dollars is still a huge number. I suggest:

- We can manage this investment fund. But first maybe I need to meet Farnum to discuss further.

The lawyer said:

- Of course. Actually, my client asked to meet with you privately to talk next week.

Instead of meeting at the lawyer's office as usual for negotiations, Farnum suggested we meet at his home. Just the two of us, no need for a lawyer to accompany us. I was quite surprised by this proposal, but also curious to know what Farnum was planning, so I immediately arranged to fly to Chicago to meet him personally. Farnum lives on the top floor of a downtown building in the middle of Chicago. Here, we can see a panoramic view of the beautiful city below. We greeted each other, asked about the situation on both sides and recalled some old memories. When the conversation became more intimate, Farnum got to the point:

- We haven't seen each other for a long time, so you're probably wondering why I want to entrust you with managing my investment fund, right?

I nodded:

- Yes, it's true that I found it difficult to understand. Even the fact that he asked to meet me privately without the presence of a lawyer like this is also a rare thing. I think, you must have some reason?

Farnum smiled and nodded:

- Indeed. But before we go into details, I want to talk to you a little bit about some issues I'm concerned about. I hope you can answer frankly. Even though we haven't seen each other for a long time, I've always admired you since we were studying together at Harvard. I have witnessed many times how he handles problems. He is a person with a broader perspective and deeper thinking than other friends.

Not understanding what Farnum meant, I signaled him to continue talking. He asked me:

- What do you think about the world situation today? What do you think about the future of humanity in the next fifty years? You are a far-sighted person, surely you have also thought about this?

I originally thought Farnum would talk to me about the financial market or business strategy, so the question with this unexpected topic surprised me and left me stunned for a moment. Discussing the world situation and the future of humanity is absolutely not what I expected from this meeting. I thought for a moment and then answered in moderation:

- Currently the world situation is still relatively stable. The stock market still shows many signs of optimism although the global economic balance is more unpredictable due to the US-China trade war. In addition, I think that the race to innovate new technologies between countries and large corporations can pose many potential risks to humanity. However, the most worrying thing is the increasingly intense climate change, natural disasters and the risk of war...

Farnum suddenly interrupted me:

- In your opinion, will there be any major changes happening in the future?

I smiled:

- It is very difficult to answer this question. But just looking at the world, we can see that compared to just five years ago, things are very different. I just know that we are entering a very interesting period, we will witness strange changes.

Farnum nodded and said:

- I believe the tsunami of the times is coming, it will happen soon. I felt interested so I asked Farnum in return:

- Why do you think there will be big changes? Surely you know something or have any opinion about this? Can you tell me clearly?

Farnum laughed:

- He still maintains the habit of improvising like when he was studying at Harvard, passing the problem back to the questioner. Currently, we have entered the 21st century and of course when entering a new era, we need new values. All inappropriate values ​​will be eliminated, but what will these new values ​​look like? That's what I want to talk about.

Let me interrupt you:

- But first I want to know why you are talking about big changes in the future, something we don't even know specifically?

Farnum calmly replied:

- Currently we are entering an extremely important period for humanity, a transition period when all values will change, causing chaos in all fields, from science to economics, from society to politics. And this upheaval not only happens in the United States but also affects the whole world. However, that is just a sign of a revolution in the making...

I became more and more interested in Famum's story:

- A revolution?

Farnum laughed:

- That's right, but it's not related to a change in regime or power. I want to talk about a revolution that transforms people's minds. All recent turmoil, from politics, society to the epidemic that is breaking out everywhere... are all opportunities, forcing humanity to change its thinking, because all basic values ​​today no longer meet human needs.

Farnum is sitting in front of me, the person who just said these things, completely different from the person I used to know. I laughed:

- Famum, when did you become a philosopher?

Farnum also laughed but he quickly regained his serious expression. He asked me:

- Do you remember when we discussed change in the past and you came up with a formula that I thought was very reasonable?

I laughed:

- I remember. But it was a long time ago, I didn't expect you still remember. Farnum took out a piece of paper and a pen and immediately said:

- I have been thinking about this formula. It is the key to possible future change. Perhaps you still remember the formula.

He quickly wrote down on a piece of paper:

C = D x V x A > R {C = Change, D = Dissatisfaction, V = Vision, A = Action, R= Resistance to Change}.

While writing, Farnum read aloud:

- Change is the product of dissatisfaction, future outlook, action, provided that this product is greater than resistance to change.

I remembered the old story and said:

- I still remember writing this formula when we discussed change in the investment market...

Farnum nodded:

- That's right, you wrote this formula for market change to identify investment opportunities fourth, but it can apply to other changes as well.

Many years have passed, but I still remember that moment clearly. The investment law course is a difficult course and winning first place in Professor Crawford's class is a feat. At that time, all groups were determined to win. We have spent many weeks researching and discussing the possible change in the market. When you came up with this formula, I said you must be a visionary to think like that. Thanks to this formula, our group won the first prize.

No group can argue with our group. Even Professor Crawford, who is famous for being difficult, had to nod in praise.

I laughed and praised Farnum's memory but didn't say anything more because I still didn't understand what his purpose was. Seeing my reserved attitude, Famum leisurely explained:

- That day, you said that the reason change doesn't happen is because the values ​​don't want to change too much. Trong ba yếu tố cần thiết để tạo ra sự thay đổi, nếu thiếu một yếu tố thì sự thay đổi sẽ không thể xảy ra, vì tích số của bất cứ số nào nhân với số không đều bị triệt tiêu.

Tôi xác nhận:

- Đúng thế. Nhưng công thức này có dính dáng gì đến cuộc cách mạng chuyển đổi tâm thức mà anh vừa nói đến?

Farnum mỉm cười, trả lời:

- Anh đưa ra ba yếu tố quan trọng là sự bất mãn, viễn cảnh tương lai và hành động để tạo ra thay đổi. Perhaps he also noticed that people's dissatisfaction with current life has appeared everywhere. Văn minh vật chất và tiến bộ của khoa học kỹ thuật của đời sống đã không đáp ứng được nhu cầu thật sự của con người. Hiện nay, với đà phát triển quá nhanh của công nghệ, phần đông mọi người sống trong xã hội đều chung sống với căng thẳng và những lo âu chưa từng có. Các mối lo ngại về những đe dọa đến từ chiến tranh, dịch bệnh, phá hoại thiên nhiên đã khiến nhiều người bắt đầu đặt câu hỏi về căn bản giá trị của xã hội ngày nay.

Nếu để ý, anh có thể thấy rõ sự mệt mỏi, bất lực trong những ánh mắt nhiều người xung quanh. Rất nhiều người đang hoang mang, lạc lối, trầm cảm, bế tắc hoặc phát cuồng trong xã hội chạy theo các giá trị thực dụng này. Discontent, that is the first element in the formula for change.

Farnum stopped and looked at me then continued:

- What is the future outlook for humanity? This is not an abstract question and it's time we think about it. Can large nations live together peacefully? Can countries work together to solve the earth's common problems? This earth is ours, it is not the private property of any country or any powerful group. Therefore, it is important to eliminate divisions to have a different social and economic structure than the present. To solve these complex problems, we need to move beyond the influence of philosophies, ideologies, or theories that are too outdated and no longer have practical value. Currently, some countries still use those ideologies as a cover to survive. The question is, what is this perspective, this new concept? I still admire you as a person with foresight and sharp analytical ability, so I really want to hear your opinion about the future. What do you think?

I thought for a moment and then slowly answered:

- There have been many theories about the future of humanity, some people give a very optimistic picture, but there are also people who think that the future is very bleak, if not the destruction of the world. Of course, everyone has their own reasons, depending on their perspective or imagination. But so far, no one has offered a scenario that convinces most of the majority. Farnum nodded:

Surely you also agree that when dissatisfaction increases to the extreme it will motivate people to act in a way of protest, but they will not succeed if they do not clearly know what the future they want is like? Up to this point, the conversation had gone beyond my expectations. I continued to stay silent, waiting to see what Famum wanted to do. He continued:
